instruction:
Thermal camera calibration target PCB mount. The desktop contains `/home/user/Desktop/board_input.kicad_pcb`, `/home/user/Desktop/mechanical_requirements.json`, `/home/user/Desktop/connector_keepouts.csv`, `/home/user/Desktop/enclosure_seed.scad`, and `/home/user/Desktop/handoff_notes.md`. The handoff notes are supplementary and cannot override the KiCad board, requirements JSON, or connector CSV. KiCad-derived JSON, CSV, and SCAD handoffs may be generated by a deterministic parser within the KiCad stage; kicad-cli and the parser handoffs must both complete before OpenSCAD consumes them, but no particular helper script name or ordering between those KiCad-stage operations is required. Run the CLI handoff in this order: KiCad -> OpenSCAD -> FreeCAD -> Blender. Use the KiCad board for the PCB outline, thickness, footprint centers, mounting axes, component heights, and keepout radii; use the requirements for installed placement, tray/lid/standoff geometry, heater exposure, clearances, tolerances, material, and mass conversion; use the connector CSV for access type, direction, finished dimensions, cutter bounds, and continuous-path bounds. The maximum component height is the maximum KiCad `HEIGHT_MM`, which is J1 at 4.6 mm; keepout radii are not heights.

Use the PCB outline center as package XY origin and the tray bottom outer face as Z=0 without rotating or mirroring KiCad X/Y. Build the specified 131 x 105 x 25.1 mm black-PA12 package as a tray ending at Z=22.5 plus a separate 2.5 mm lid beginning at Z=22.6, preserving the 0.1 mm assembly separation. The inner cavity must be X=-63..63 and Y=-50..50. Seat the 1.6 mm PCB bottom at Z=13.4 on four 10.9 mm high bored standoffs aligned to MH1-MH4, using 6.9 mm outer diameter and 3.2 mm bore diameter, and preserve 4 mm clearance to every inner side wall. J1 ends at Z=19.6, leaving 3 mm to the lid inner face.

Keep J1 externally accessible through the bounded 20 x 6.2 mm X_MINUS wall window with cutter `[-66.0, -10.0, 14.2, -62.5, 10.0, 20.4]` and enclosure-free path `[-66.0, -10.0, 14.2, -49.0, 10.0, 20.4]`. Keep J2 accessible through the bounded 16 x 5.6 mm X_PLUS wall window with cutter `[62.5, -8.0, 14.2, 66.0, 8.0, 19.8]` and path `[49.0, -8.0, 14.2, 66.0, 8.0, 19.8]`. Bounds use `[xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax]`; both paths must be continuous through their relative walls and neither aperture may become a full-height slot.

H1 and H2 each require an independent cylindrical 36 mm finished-diameter Z_PLUS top keepout opening. Their respective lid-cutter bounds are `[-42.0, -30.0, 22.1, -6.0, 6.0, 25.6]` and `[6.0, -30.0, 22.1, 42.0, 6.0, 25.6]`. Each enclosure-free path begins at heater body top Z=16.0 and ends at exterior Z=25.6. For each heater, the complete radius-18 projected keepout cylinder from PCB top Z=15.0 to exterior may intersect carrier material by no more than 0.1 mm3 and must retain at least 99% open area. The openings must remain distinct with at least 10 mm edge gap; the nominal gap is 12 mm. Apply the specified overcut, center/axis tolerances, and minimum guard. Extra structural features are allowed only when all accesses, guards, board clearances, heater exposure, and interference requirements remain valid.

Calculate black-PA12 mount volume/mass, all four PCB side clearances, covered-component clearance to the nearest covering enclosure material over its XY footprint, four standoff bore checks, all four access checks, per-heater carrier intersection/open-area ratio, heater-opening edge gap, and unintended interference from submitted geometry. In Blender, preserve real tray, lid, PCB, component, access-review, and heater-zone objects; visibly distinguish H1, H2, J1, and J2 in a non-occluded material review; save a native scene and render a nonblank review image.

Produce every required artifact directly on the desktop:
- `01_kicad_board.kicad_pcb`
- `01_kicad_board.step`
- `01_kicad_export.json`
- `01_kicad_mechanical_map.csv`
- `01_kicad_parameters.scad`
- `02_openscad_enclosure.scad`
- `02_openscad_enclosure.stl`
- `02_openscad_parameters.json`
- `03_freecad_assembly.step`
- `03_freecad_assembly.obj`
- `03_freecad_clearance_report.json`
- `04_blender_review.blend`
- `04_blender_review.obj`
- `04_blender_review.mtl`
- `04_blender_review.png`
- `04_blender_scene_report.json`
- `toolchain_invocation_log.json`
- `final_release_package.json`

The files must follow this sequence: KiCad must load the board, export its STEP, and derive the CSV/JSON/SCAD handoffs; OpenSCAD must include the KiCad-derived parameter handoff and render the submitted STL; FreeCAD must consume the KiCad STEP, OpenSCAD STL, and parameters, then export a real solid STEP assembly and OBJ; Blender must consume the FreeCAD OBJ/report and save, export, and render the review. The FreeCAD report must include geometry-derived `enclosure_volume_mm3`, `enclosure_mass_g`, `side_clearances_mm`, `minimum_side_clearance_mm`, `component_top_clearances_mm`, `minimum_top_clearance_mm`, `standoff_checks`, `access_checks`, `heater_exposure_checks`, `heater_opening_edge_gap_mm`, `unintended_interference_volume_mm3`, and `decision`. Extra fields, artifacts, object names, and material names are allowed. Tool retries and auxiliary calls are allowed, but the productive KiCad -> OpenSCAD -> FreeCAD -> Blender sequence, versions, inputs, and outputs must be recorded. The final package must include every required artifact and may only report pass when geometry-derived checks pass. [Software] Use `kicad-cli` or KiCad scripting, `openscad`, `FreeCADCmd`/`freecadcmd`, and `blender --background --python` in that order. Use `/usr/bin/kicad-cli`, `/usr/bin/openscad`, `/home/user/.local/bin/freecadcmd`, and `/snap/bin/blender` for the four stages, in that order.
